pgi_001: You can recognise it by being the largest thing in the cloister by a wide margin, with lightning scars still visible on the trunk. It stands in the cloister of Palazzo Murena.
pgi_002: You can recognise it by standing at the top of Corso Vannucci, on the terrace edge looking over the valley, beside a red fir of similar age. It stands in Piazza Italia.
pgi_003: You can recognise it by its squat shape for such a thick trunk, its limbs held by elastic guy wires and bracing. It stands in front of the Ciabatti Montessori school, Porta Pesa.
pgi_004: You can recognise it as the taller of Perugia's two cedars of Lebanon, 18 metres against the other's 12.5. It stands at Largo della Croce Rossa, Via Masi.
pgi_005: You can recognise it by its smooth grey bark, like a beech's, growing straight out of the street paving rather than a garden. It stands on Via Fiume.
pgi_007: You can recognise it by standing over the cemetery's gravel avenues and cypresses, next to the Templar church of San Bevignate. It stands in the Cimitero Monumentale.
pgi_008: You can recognise it by its narrow, columnar shape, the closest monumental tree to the centre of Perugia. It stands in Parco della Cuparella, along the city walls.
